name: Edge router
kid: The front door of the data centre. It lets parcels in from the exchange and sends the video back out.
nerd: The PoP’s edge router: it peers over BGP at the exchange, announcing the video company’s addresses, and routes into the fabric, spreading traffic over the load balancers.

1995.name: Router
1995.kid: The server room’s front door. The rented line from the big network ends here, and the page goes back out the same way.
1995.nerd: The hosting site’s router: the T1 from the backbone’s PoP ends on a serial port (Cisco HDLC), with a static default route back up it. A site this small has no BGP of its own.

2010.name: Core router
2010.nerd: The core router of the video company’s cage: it peers over BGP at the exchange, announcing the company’s addresses, and routes down over 10G to the load balancer and the aggregation switches.
